explanation: The person Krishna describes does not need to flee the world. Instead, the senses remain disciplined and neither liking nor dislike controls the mind.

source.sanskrit:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन्।

आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति।।2.64।।
source.transliteration:
rāga-dveṣha-viyuktais tu viṣhayān indriyaiśh charan
ātma-vaśhyair-vidheyātmā prasādam adhigachchhati
source.translation: But the self-controlled man, moving among objects with the senses restrained and free from attraction and repulsion, attains peace.

simpleVersion: Krishna says that in this peaceful state, suffering falls away and the tranquil mind becomes steady.
explanation: Krishna describes the result of inner peace: suffering is diminished and the intellect of the tranquil person becomes firmly established.

source.sanskrit:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते।

प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते।।2.65।।
source.transliteration:
prasāde sarva-duḥkhānāṁ hānir asyopajāyate
prasanna-chetaso hyāśhu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣhṭhate
source.translation: In that peace, all pains are destroyed; for the intellect of the tranquil-minded soon becomes steady.

hook: Without inner steadiness, where can lasting peace come from?
simpleVersion: Krishna connects an unsteady mind to the absence of meditation, peace, and lasting happiness.
explanation: Krishna presents a chain in the opposite direction from the earlier one: without steadiness there is no deep contemplation, without contemplation there is no peace, and without peace there is no happiness.

source.sanskrit:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना।

न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम्।।2.66।।
source.transliteration:
nāsti buddhir-ayuktasya na chāyuktasya bhāvanā
na chābhāvayataḥ śhāntir aśhāntasya kutaḥ sukham
source.translation: There is no knowledge of the Self for the unsteady, and no meditation is possible for the unsteady, and no peace for the unmeditative, and how can there be happiness for one who has no peace?

hook: If your attention follows every impulse, your judgment can be carried off course.
simpleVersion: Krishna compares a mind following wandering senses to a boat blown off course by the wind.
explanation: The image shows how easily judgment can be lost when the mind follows every sensory impulse. Like a boat pushed by wind, it can drift far from its intended direction.

source.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते।

तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि।।2.67।।
source.transliteration:
indriyāṇāṁ hi charatāṁ yan mano ’nuvidhīyate
tadasya harati prajñāṁ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi
source.translation: For the mind, which follows in the wake of the wandering senses, carries away his discrimination, as the wind carries away a boat on the waters.

simpleVersion: Krishna says the person whose senses are fully restrained has steady wisdom.
explanation: Krishna restates the central point: steady wisdom belongs to the person who has brought the senses under control rather than allowing them to chase their objects.

source.sanskrit:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.68।।
source.transliteration:
tasmād yasya mahā-bāho nigṛihītāni sarvaśhaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
source.translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed Arjuna, his knowledge is steady whose senses are completely restrained from sense objects.

hook: The wise may be awake to something most people never notice.
simpleVersion: Krishna describes a reversal of perspective: what is unseen by ordinary people is where the disciplined person is awake, while ordinary concerns are like night to the sage.
explanation: Krishna presents the wise person's awareness as different from ordinary attention. What most people overlook can be vivid to the disciplined sage, while common pursuits may hold little attraction for them.

source.sanskrit:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी।

यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः।।2.69।।
source.transliteration:
yā niśhā sarva-bhūtānāṁ tasyāṁ jāgarti sanyamī
yasyāṁ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśhā paśhyato muneḥ
source.translation: That which is night to all beings, in that the self-controlled man is awake; when all beings are awake, that is night for the sage who sees.

hook: Can you receive what comes without becoming restless for more?
simpleVersion: Krishna compares the peaceful person to an ocean that remains full and unmoved as rivers enter it; craving, by contrast, prevents peace.
explanation: The ocean image describes someone who can receive experiences and desires without being overwhelmed by them. Krishna contrasts this with the person who remains driven by craving.

source.sanskrit:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं

समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।

तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे

स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी।।2.70।।
source.transliteration:
āpūryamāṇam achala-pratiṣhṭhaṁ
samudram āpaḥ praviśhanti yadvat
tadvat kāmā yaṁ praviśhanti sarve
sa śhāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī
source.translation: He attains peace into whom all desires enter, just as waters enter the ocean which, filled from all sides, remains unmoved; but not the man who is full of desires.

hook: Peace grows when desire no longer owns you.
simpleVersion: Krishna says the person who moves through life without craving, possessiveness, or ego attains peace.
explanation: Krishna summarizes the qualities that lead to peace: giving up desires, letting go of possessiveness, and releasing egoistic identification.

source.sanskrit:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः।

निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति।।2.71।।
source.transliteration:
vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumānśh charati niḥspṛihaḥ
nirmamo nirahankāraḥ sa śhāntim adhigachchhati
source.translation: That person attains peace who, abandoning all desires, moves about without longing, without the sense of ownership, and without egoism.

hook: The goal is not just to survive confusion, but to become free from it.
simpleVersion: Krishna concludes that the person who reaches this Brahmic state is no longer deluded and can attain union with Brahman even at the end of life.
explanation: Krishna calls this state Brahmic and says that once it is attained, delusion ends. Remaining established in it leads to the liberation described as union with Brahman.

source.sanskrit:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।

स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति।।2.72।।
source.transliteration:
eṣhā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṁ prāpya vimuhyati
sthitvāsyām anta-kāle ’pi brahma-nirvāṇam ṛichchhati
source.translation: O son of Pritha, this is the eternal state, the Brahmic seat. Attaining this, one is not deluded. Being established in it, one attains oneness with Brahman even at the end of life.

simpleVersion: Arjuna asks Krishna why he's being pushed into terrible action if knowledge is supposedly superior to action.
explanation: Confused by what he's just heard, Arjuna challenges Krishna. If knowledge is really the higher path, he asks, why is Krishna urging him toward the terrible action of war instead?

source.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन।

तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव।।3.1।।
source.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
jyāyasī chet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana
tat kiṁ karmaṇi ghore māṁ niyojayasi keśhava
source.translation: Arjuna said: If Thou thinkest that knowledge is superior to action, O Krishna, why then, O Kesava, doest Thou ask me to engage in this terrible action?

simpleVersion: Arjuna says Krishna's mixed words are confusing him, and asks for one clear answer about what will truly help him.
explanation: Arjuna admits he's genuinely lost. He tells Krishna that his teaching so far feels contradictory, and asks for a single, definite answer about the one path that will actually lead to his good.

source.sanskrit:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे।

तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम्।।3.2।।
source.transliteration:
vyāmiśhreṇeva vākyena buddhiṁ mohayasīva me
tad ekaṁ vada niśhchitya yena śhreyo ’ham āpnuyām
source.translation: With this seemingly perplexing speech, you seem to be confusing my understanding; therefore, tell me one certain way by which I may attain bliss.

simpleVersion: Krishna says there are two paths in this world: the path of knowledge for the contemplative, and the path of action for the active.
explanation: Krishna answers Arjuna's confusion by clarifying that he had already described two distinct paths: one built on knowledge, suited to contemplative seekers, and one built on action, suited to those who engage with the world.

source.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ।

ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम्।।3.3।।
source.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
loke’smin dvi-vidhā niṣhṭhā purā proktā mayānagha
jñāna-yogena sāṅkhyānāṁ karma-yogena yoginām
source.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "In this world, there is a twofold path, as I said before, O sinless one: the path of knowledge of the Sankhyas and the path of action of the Yogins."

simpleVersion: Krishna says a person doesn't reach freedom from action just by avoiding action, nor reach perfection through mere renunciation.
explanation: Krishna corrects a common misunderstanding. Simply refusing to act is not the same as true spiritual freedom, and giving up outward activity alone does not automatically bring inner perfection.

source.sanskrit:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते।

न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति।।3.4।।
source.transliteration:
na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣhkarmyaṁ puruṣho ’śhnute
na cha sannyasanād eva siddhiṁ samadhigachchhati
source.translation: Man does not reach actionlessness by not performing actions; nor does he attain perfection by mere renunciation.

simpleVersion: Krishna says no one can stay without acting even for a moment, since everyone is compelled to act by the qualities of nature.
explanation: Krishna points out a basic fact of human existence: action is unavoidable. The forces of nature within every person compel them to act constantly, whether they intend to or not.

source.sanskrit:
न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्।

कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः।।3.5।।
source.transliteration:
na hi kaśhchit kṣhaṇam api jātu tiṣhṭhatyakarma-kṛit
kāryate hyavaśhaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛiti-jair guṇaiḥ
source.translation: Verily, no one can remain for even a moment without performing action; for everyone is made to act helplessly, indeed, by the qualities born of Nature.

simpleVersion: Krishna says someone who restrains their body from acting but keeps thinking about sense objects in their mind is just fooling themselves.
explanation: Krishna warns against a kind of false discipline. A person who physically holds back from action but mentally keeps dwelling on desires isn't actually practicing self-control, just deceiving themselves and others.

source.sanskrit:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्।

इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते।।3.6।।
source.transliteration:
karmendriyāṇi sanyamya ya āste manasā smaran
indriyārthān vimūḍhātmā mithyāchāraḥ sa uchyate
source.translation: He who, restraining the organs of action, sits thinking of the sense-objects in his mind, he of deluded understanding is called a hypocrite.

simpleVersion: Krishna says the one who uses the mind to guide the senses and acts without attachment through disciplined action is far better.
explanation: Krishna contrasts this with real discipline. Someone who consciously directs their senses through the mind, then engages in action without clinging to it, is genuinely practicing a superior form of self-mastery.

source.sanskrit:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन।

कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते।।3.7।।
source.transliteration:
yas tvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate ’rjuna
karmendriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ sa viśhiṣhyate
source.translation: But whoever, controlling the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, engages himself in Karma Yoga with the organs of action, without attachment, he excels.

simpleVersion: Krishna tells Arjuna to perform his prescribed duty, since action is better than inaction, and even keeping the body alive requires action.
explanation: Krishna gives Arjuna a direct, practical instruction: fulfill the duty assigned to him. Action is inherently better than inaction, and even something as basic as sustaining one's own body requires acting in the world.
lifeLesson: Even survival itself depends on action; total inaction isn't really an option for anyone alive.

source.sanskrit:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः।

शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः।।3.8।।
source.transliteration:
niyataṁ kuru karma tvaṁ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ
śharīra-yātrāpi cha te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ
source.translation: Perform your bounden duty, for action is superior to inaction, and even the maintenance of the body would not be possible for you through inaction.

simpleVersion: Krishna says the world is bound by selfish action, so Arjuna should act selflessly, as an offering, free from personal attachment.
explanation: Krishna introduces the idea of sacrificial action. Ordinary self-serving action creates bondage, but action performed as an offering, done without personal attachment, does not tie a person down in the same way.

source.sanskrit:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः।

तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर।।3.9।।
source.transliteration:
yajñārthāt karmaṇo ’nyatra loko ’yaṁ karma-bandhanaḥ
tad-arthaṁ karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgaḥ samāchara
source.translation: The world is bound by actions other than those performed for the sake of sacrifice; do thou, therefore, O son of Kunti (Arjuna), perform actions for that sake alone, free from attachment.

simpleVersion: Krishna says the Creator, when making humanity, paired it with sacrifice, telling people this would provide for all their needs and desires.
explanation: Krishna offers a mythic explanation for why selfless action matters. From the very beginning, humanity was created alongside the principle of sacrifice, meant to sustain people and fulfill their needs when practiced rightly.

source.sanskrit:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः।

अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक्।।3.10।।
source.transliteration:
saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛiṣhṭvā purovācha prajāpatiḥ
anena prasaviṣhyadhvam eṣha vo ’stviṣhṭa-kāma-dhuk
source.translation: The Creator, having in the beginning created mankind together with sacrifice, said, "By this shall you propagate; let this be the milch cow of your desires—the cow that yields all the desired objects."

simpleVersion: Krishna says by nourishing the gods through sacrifice, the gods will nourish humanity in return, and this mutual care leads to the highest good.
explanation: Krishna describes a reciprocal relationship built on giving. When people support the divine order through their sacrificial actions, that same order supports them back, and this exchange leads toward genuine wellbeing.

source.sanskrit:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः।

परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ।।3.11।।
source.transliteration:
devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ
parasparaṁ bhāvayantaḥ śhreyaḥ param avāpsyatha
source.translation: With this, nourish the gods, and may the gods nourish you; thus, nourishing each other, you shall attain the highest good.

simpleVersion: Krishna says the gods, sustained by sacrifice, provide what people desire, and anyone who enjoys these gifts without giving back is essentially a thief.
explanation: Krishna frames unearned enjoyment as a kind of theft. Since the gods provide for people because of sacrifice, taking those gifts without offering anything back breaks the reciprocal relationship entirely.

source.sanskrit:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।

तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः।।3.12।।
source.transliteration:
iṣhṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ
tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
source.translation: The gods, nourished by the sacrifice, will give you the desired objects. So, he who enjoys the objects given by the gods without offering anything in return is indeed a thief.

simpleVersion: Krishna says the righteous who eat only after offering sacrifice are freed from sin, while those who cook only for themselves eat sin.
explanation: Krishna draws a moral distinction around a simple daily act, eating. Those who act with a spirit of offering and sharing remain free of wrongdoing, while those who act purely for self-interest bear the consequences.

source.sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः।

भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्।।3.13।।
source.transliteration:
yajña-śhiṣhṭāśhinaḥ santo muchyante sarva-kilbiṣhaiḥ
bhuñjate te tvaghaṁ pāpā ye pachantyātma-kāraṇāt
source.translation: The righteous who eat the remnants of the sacrifice are freed from all sins; but those sinful ones who cook food solely for their own sake indeed consume sin.

simpleVersion: Krishna traces a chain: beings come from food, food comes from rain, rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice comes from action.
explanation: Krishna lays out a cosmic chain of dependency. Life depends on food, food depends on rain, rain depends on sacrifice, and sacrifice itself depends on human action, tying everything back to how people choose to act.

source.sanskrit:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।

यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः।।3.14।।
source.transliteration:
annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād anna-sambhavaḥ
yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ
source.translation: From food come forth beings; from rain, food is produced; from sacrifice arises rain, and sacrifice is born of action.

simpleVersion: Krishna says action originates from Brahman, and Brahman from the Imperishable, so the all-pervading Brahman is always present within sacrifice.
explanation: Krishna traces the chain of the previous verse back to its ultimate source. Action itself flows from Brahman, which flows from the eternal, so the sacred is woven into the very structure of right action.

source.sanskrit:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्।

तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्।।3.15।।
source.transliteration:
karma brahmodbhavaṁ viddhi brahmākṣhara-samudbhavam
tasmāt sarva-gataṁ brahma nityaṁ yajñe pratiṣhṭhitam
source.translation: Know that action comes from Brahma, and Brahma comes from the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervasive Brahma ever rests in sacrifice.

simpleVersion: Krishna says whoever doesn't follow this cycle of sacrifice, but lives only chasing the senses, is living a wasted, sinful life.
explanation: Krishna warns of the consequences of ignoring this natural order. A person who breaks away from this cycle of mutual giving and instead lives purely to indulge the senses is, in his words, living pointlessly.

source.sanskrit:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः।

अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति।।3.16।।
source.transliteration:
evaṁ pravartitaṁ chakraṁ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ
aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṁ pārtha sa jīvati
source.translation: He who does not follow the wheel thus set in motion, who is of sinful life, rejoicing in the senses, lives in vain, O Arjuna.

simpleVersion: Krishna says a person who finds joy, satisfaction, and contentment entirely within the Self has nothing left that they truly need to do.
explanation: Krishna introduces an important exception. Someone who has found complete inner fulfillment, delighting in and satisfied by the Self alone, is no longer bound by the same obligations that govern everyone else's action.

source.sanskrit:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः।

आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते।।3.17।।
source.transliteration:
yas tvātma-ratir eva syād ātma-tṛiptaśh cha mānavaḥ
ātmanyeva cha santuṣhṭas tasya kāryaṁ na vidyate
source.translation: But for that man who rejoices only in the Self, who is satisfied with the Self and is content in the Self alone, indeed there is nothing to do.

simpleVersion: Krishna says such a person gains nothing from acting and loses nothing from not acting, and doesn't depend on any being for any purpose.
explanation: Krishna elaborates on the state of the self-fulfilled person. For them, action and inaction make no real difference, and they have no dependence on anyone else in the world for their own sense of purpose.

source.sanskrit:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन।

न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः।।3.18।।
source.transliteration:
naiva tasya kṛitenārtho nākṛiteneha kaśhchana
na chāsya sarva-bhūteṣhu kaśhchid artha-vyapāśhrayaḥ
source.translation: For him, there is no interest whatsoever in what is done or not done; nor does he depend on any being for any purpose.

simpleVersion: Krishna tells Arjuna to keep performing his required actions without attachment, since acting this way leads a person to the Supreme.
explanation: Krishna returns to practical instruction for Arjuna, who is not yet in that fully self-contented state. He should continue performing necessary duties, but without clinging to them, since this kind of unattached action leads toward ultimate fulfillment.

source.sanskrit:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।

असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः।।3.19।।
source.transliteration:
tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samāchara
asakto hyācharan karma param āpnoti pūruṣhaḥ
source.translation: Therefore, without attachment, always perform the actions that should be done; for by performing actions without attachment, one reaches the Supreme.

simpleVersion: Krishna says figures like King Janaka reached perfection purely through action, so Arjuna should also act with the wellbeing of others in mind.
explanation: Krishna offers a historical example to back up his teaching. Great figures like Janaka reached spiritual perfection simply by acting rightly, and Arjuna is urged to act similarly, with the wider good of people in view.

source.sanskrit:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः।

लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि।।3.20।।
source.transliteration:
karmaṇaiva hi sansiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ
loka-saṅgraham evāpi sampaśhyan kartum arhasi
source.translation: Janaka and others attained perfection indeed through action alone; even with the intention of protecting the masses, you should perform action.

simpleVersion: Krishna says whatever a great or respected person does, others naturally follow, and whatever example they set becomes the standard people copy.
explanation: Krishna highlights the influence of visible leaders. Ordinary people tend to imitate whatever a respected figure does, meaning that person's actions quietly become a model that shapes everyone else's behavior.
lifeLesson: The example you set, especially if others look up to you, often matters more than any instructions you could give.

source.sanskrit:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः।

स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते।।3.21।।
source.transliteration:
yad yad ācharati śhreṣhṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate
source.translation: Whatever a great man does, others also do; whatever he establishes as the standard, the world follows.

simpleVersion: Krishna says there's nothing in all three worlds He personally needs to do, or hasn't already attained, yet He still continues to act.
explanation: Krishna uses Himself as an example. Despite having nothing left to gain or accomplish anywhere in existence, He continues to engage in action anyway, demonstrating that action doesn't always come from personal need.

source.sanskrit:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन।

नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि।।3.22।।
source.transliteration:
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṁ triṣhu lokeṣhu kiñchana
nānavāptam avāptavyaṁ varta eva cha karmaṇi
source.translation: There is nothing in the three worlds, O Arjuna, that needs to be done by Me, nor is there anything unattained that needs to be attained; yet I engage Myself in action.

simpleVersion: Krishna says if He ever stopped acting, tirelessly engaged in His work, people everywhere would end up following His example and stop too.
explanation: Krishna explains His reason for continuing to act despite having nothing to gain: as someone others look up to, if He were to become idle, people across the world would follow that same example.

source.sanskrit:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।

मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।3.23।।
source.transliteration:
yadi hyahaṁ na varteyaṁ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣhyāḥ pārtha sarvaśhaḥ
source.translation: For, should I not ever engage myself in action, unwearied, people would in every way follow my path, O Arjuna.

simpleVersion: Krishna says if He stopped performing His actions, these worlds would fall apart, and He would cause chaos and destruction among all beings.
explanation: Krishna underscores the stakes of His own example. If He were to abandon action, the resulting collapse of order would be severe, leading to widespread confusion and harm across all of creation.

source.sanskrit:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्।

सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः।।3.24।।
source.transliteration:
utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṁ karma ched aham
sankarasya cha kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ
source.translation: These worlds would perish if I did not perform action; I would be the author of confusion of castes and destruction of these beings.

simpleVersion: Krishna says just as the ignorant act out of attachment, the wise should act without attachment, but still act, for the good of the world.
explanation: Krishna draws a clear parallel and distinction. Both the ignorant and the wise remain active, but where the ignorant act out of personal craving, the wise act with detachment, motivated instead by a wish to benefit the world.

source.sanskrit:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत।

कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्िचकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम्।।3.25।।
source.transliteration:
saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvānso yathā kurvanti bhārata
kuryād vidvāns tathāsaktaśh chikīrṣhur loka-saṅgraham
source.translation: As the ignorant act out of attachment to action, O Bharata, so should the wise act without attachment, wishing for the welfare of the world.

simpleVersion: Krishna says a wise person shouldn't confuse or unsettle people who are still attached to action, but should instead guide them by working alongside them.
explanation: Krishna gives practical guidance on how the wise should relate to others who aren't as advanced. Rather than disrupting their sense of purpose, the wise person should engage in action too, quietly setting a helpful example instead.
lifeLesson: Real wisdom often shows up as patience with others rather than correcting them outright.

source.sanskrit:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्।

जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन्।।3.26।।
source.transliteration:
na buddhi-bhedaṁ janayed ajñānāṁ karma-saṅginām
joṣhayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācharan
source.translation: Let no wise man unsettle the minds of ignorant people who are attached to action; he should engage them in all actions, himself fulfilling them with devotion.

simpleVersion: Krishna explains that all actions are actually carried out by nature's inherent qualities, though the ego-deluded mind believes 'I am the doer.'
explanation: Krishna reveals a subtler truth about action. In reality, the underlying forces of nature are what drive all activity; it's only the ego, caught in delusion, that mistakenly claims personal ownership over these actions.

source.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः।

अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते।।3.27।।
source.transliteration:
prakṛiteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśhaḥ
ahankāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate
source.translation: All actions are wrought in all cases by the qualities of Nature alone. He whose mind is deluded by egoism thinks, "I am the doer."

simpleVersion: Krishna says one who truly understands how nature's qualities and actions divide up doesn't get attached, seeing it as forces simply interacting with forces.
explanation: Krishna contrasts this with genuine understanding. A person who sees clearly how the qualities of nature act upon each other realizes that no personal self is really doing anything, and so remains free from attachment.

source.sanskrit:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः।

गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते।।3.28।।
source.transliteration:
tattva-vit tu mahā-bāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ
guṇā guṇeṣhu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
source.translation: But he who knows the Truth, O mighty-armed Arjuna, about the divisions of the qualities and their functions, knowing that the Gunas, as senses, move amidst the Gunas, as the sense-objects, is not attached.

simpleVersion: Krishna says those confused by nature's qualities become attached to their functions, and the wise person shouldn't unsettle these less knowledgeable people.
explanation: Krishna advises patience toward those who don't yet see this truth. People deluded by nature's forces naturally cling to activity, and someone with fuller understanding shouldn't disturb their limited but sincere engagement with the world.

source.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु।

तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत्।।3.29।।
source.transliteration:
prakṛiter guṇa-sammūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu
tān akṛitsna-vido mandān kṛitsna-vin na vichālayet
source.translation: Those deluded by the qualities of Nature are attached to the functions of the qualities. The man of perfect knowledge should not unsettle the foolish one who is of imperfect knowledge.

simpleVersion: Krishna tells Arjuna to offer all actions to Him, mind fixed on the Self, free of desire and ego, and fight without distress.
explanation: Krishna returns to direct instruction for Arjuna's specific moment. He should mentally surrender every action to Krishna, act without craving results or claiming personal ownership, and move forward into battle without inner turmoil.

source.sanskrit:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा।

निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः।।3.30।।
source.transliteration:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi sannyasyādhyātma-chetasā
nirāśhīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ
source.translation: Renouncing all actions in Me, with the mind centered on the Self, free from hope and egoism, and from mental fever, fight thou.

simpleVersion: Krishna says those who follow this teaching with faith and without complaint are also freed from the binding effects of action.
explanation: Krishna promises a result for those who take this teaching seriously. People who practice it consistently, with genuine faith and without resentment or cynicism, are likewise released from action's usual binding consequences.

source.sanskrit:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः।

श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः।।3.31।।
source.transliteration:
ye me matam idaṁ nityam anutiṣhṭhanti mānavāḥ
śhraddhāvanto ’nasūyanto muchyante te ’pi karmabhiḥ
source.translation: Those who constantly practice this teaching of Mine with faith and without caviling, they too are freed from actions.

simpleVersion: Krishna warns that those who criticize this teaching and refuse to follow it are lost in confusion, without discernment, and headed for ruin.
explanation: Krishna also states the consequence for the opposite response. Those who reject and mock this teaching, choosing not to practice it, remain trapped in confusion and are described as heading toward their own downfall.

source.sanskrit:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम्।

सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः।।3.32।।
source.transliteration:
ye tvetad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣhṭhanti me matam
sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhāns tān viddhi naṣhṭān achetasaḥ
source.translation: But those who criticize My teaching and do not practice it, deprived of all knowledge and lacking discernment, know them to be doomed to destruction.

simpleVersion: Krishna says even a wise person acts according to their own nature, since all beings follow nature, so what can forced restraint do?
explanation: Krishna makes a realistic observation about human nature. Even someone with wisdom will act in line with their inherent tendencies, since nature reliably asserts itself, making forced suppression largely ineffective.

source.sanskrit:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि।

प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति।।3.33।।
source.transliteration:
sadṛiśhaṁ cheṣhṭate svasyāḥ prakṛiter jñānavān api
prakṛitiṁ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṁ kariṣhyati
source.translation: Even a wise man acts in accordance with his own nature; beings will follow their nature; what can restraint do?

simpleVersion: Krishna warns that attraction and aversion arise in the senses, and Arjuna shouldn't be ruled by either, since they are his enemies.
explanation: Krishna identifies the real danger to watch for: not the senses themselves, but the automatic pull of liking and disliking that arises around them. He warns Arjuna not to let these two forces control him.

source.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ।

तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ।।3.34।।
source.transliteration:
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāga-dveṣhau vyavasthitau
tayor na vaśham āgachchhet tau hyasya paripanthinau
source.translation: Attachment and aversion for the objects of the senses abide in the senses; let no one come under their sway; for, they are his enemies.

simpleVersion: Krishna says it's better to imperfectly do one's own duty than perfectly perform someone else's; even dying in it is safer than another's.
explanation: Krishna makes an important point about personal duty. Even an imperfect attempt at one's own responsibilities is more valuable and safer than excelling at duties that were never meant to be yours in the first place.
lifeLesson: Trying to live someone else's version of a 'good life' rarely works out as well as showing up honestly for your own.

source.sanskrit:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।

स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः।।3.35।।
source.transliteration:
śhreyān swa-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣhṭhitāt
swa-dharme nidhanaṁ śhreyaḥ para-dharmo bhayāvahaḥ
source.translation: Better is one's own duty, though devoid of merit, than the duty of another well discharged. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with fear.

simpleVersion: Arjuna asks Krishna what actually drives a person to commit sin, even against their own will, as if pushed by some outside force.
explanation: Curious about human weakness, Arjuna asks a very human question: why do people end up doing wrong things even when they don't want to, almost as though they were being forced into it against their will?

source.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः।

अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः।।3.36।।
source.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
atha kena prayukto ’yaṁ pāpaṁ charati pūruṣhaḥ
anichchhann api vārṣhṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ
source.translation: Arjuna said, "But what compels man to commit sin, even against his wishes, O Varshneya (Krishna), as if constrained by force?"

simpleVersion: Krishna answers that it is desire and anger, born from restless energy, that drive people to sin; He names this as the true enemy.
explanation: Krishna gives a direct answer to Arjuna's question. The real culprit behind wrongdoing is desire, which turns into anger when frustrated, both arising from restless, agitated energy. He names this combination as humanity's true enemy.

source.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः।

महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम्।।3.37।।
source.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
kāma eṣha krodha eṣha rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ
mahāśhano mahā-pāpmā viddhyenam iha vairiṇam
source.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "It is desire and it is anger, both of the quality of Rajas, all-devouring and all-sinful; know this as the foe here in this world."

simpleVersion: Krishna compares this to fire covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by its covering: wisdom is covered by desire.
explanation: Krishna uses three everyday images to explain how desire obscures wisdom: fire wrapped in smoke, a mirror dulled by dust, and an embryo enclosed within its covering. In each case, something clear is veiled by something else.

source.sanskrit:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च।

यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम्।।3.38।।
source.transliteration:
dhūmenāvriyate vahnir yathādarśho malena cha
yatholbenāvṛito garbhas tathā tenedam āvṛitam
source.translation: As fire is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror is covered by dust, and as an embryo is surrounded by the amniotic sac, so is this enveloped by that.

simpleVersion: Krishna says wisdom is covered by this constant enemy in the form of desire, an insatiable force as impossible to fully satisfy as fire.
explanation: Krishna continues the fire imagery from before. Desire acts as wisdom's permanent enemy, and like a fire that consumes whatever feeds it without ever being satisfied, desire can never truly be fulfilled by giving in to it.

source.sanskrit:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा।

कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च।।3.39।।
source.transliteration:
āvṛitaṁ jñānam etena jñānino nitya-vairiṇā
kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣhpūreṇānalena cha
source.translation: O Arjuna, wisdom is enveloped by this constant enemy of the wise, in the form of desire, which is insatiable like fire.

simpleVersion: Krishna says desire operates through the senses, mind, and intellect, using them to delude a person and cover up their true wisdom.
explanation: Krishna identifies exactly where desire takes hold. It works through a person's senses, mind, and intellect, using these very faculties meant for understanding as its tools to create confusion and hide true wisdom instead.

source.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते।

एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम्।।3.40।।
source.transliteration:
indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣhṭhānam uchyate
etair vimohayatyeṣha jñānam āvṛitya dehinam
source.translation: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be its seat; through these, it deludes the embodied one, veiling their wisdom.

simpleVersion: Krishna tells Arjuna to first control his senses, then destroy this sinful force that damages both knowledge and true understanding.
explanation: Krishna gives Arjuna a clear plan of action. He should begin by mastering his senses, since that gives him the leverage needed to confront and overcome desire, which otherwise corrodes both knowledge and deeper understanding.

source.sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ।

पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम्।।3.41।।
source.transliteration:
tasmāt tvam indriyāṇyādau niyamya bharatarṣhabha
pāpmānaṁ prajahi hyenaṁ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśhanam
source.translation: Therefore, O best of the Bharatas, control your senses first and then kill this sinful thing, which destroys knowledge and realization.

simpleVersion: Krishna says the senses are subtle, the mind subtler than the senses, the intellect subtler than the mind, and the Self beyond intellect.
explanation: Krishna maps out a hierarchy of subtlety within a person. Moving inward from the physical senses to the mind, then to the intellect, each level is progressively finer, until reaching the Self, which stands beyond all of them.

source.sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः।

मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः।।3.42।।
source.transliteration:
indriyāṇi parāṇyāhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṁ manaḥ
manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ
source.translation: They say that the senses are superior to the body; the mind is superior to the senses; the intellect is superior to the mind; and He (the Self) is superior even to the intellect.

simpleVersion: Krishna tells Arjuna to know the Self beyond intellect, steady himself through the Self, and conquer the difficult enemy in the form of desire.
explanation: Krishna closes the chapter with a final instruction. By recognizing the Self that exists beyond even the intellect, and using that awareness to steady the mind, Arjuna is urged to finally overcome the persistent enemy of desire.

source.sanskrit:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना।

जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम्।।3.43।।
source.transliteration:
evaṁ buddheḥ paraṁ buddhvā sanstabhyātmānam ātmanā
jahi śhatruṁ mahā-bāho kāma-rūpaṁ durāsadam
source.translation: Thus, knowing Him who is superior to the intellect and restraining the self by the Self, slay thou, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the enemy in the form of desire, hard to conquer.

simpleVersion: Krishna says this timeless Yoga was first taught to Vivasvan, then passed from Vivasvan to Manu and from Manu to Ikshvaku.
explanation: Krishna explains that the Yoga he is teaching is ancient and imperishable. He says he first taught it to Vivasvan, the Sun-god. Vivasvan passed it to Manu, and Manu passed it to King Ikshvaku. The verse introduces a lineage through which this teaching was transmitted.

source.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम्।

विवस्वान् मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत्।।4.1।।
source.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
imaṁ vivasvate yogaṁ proktavān aham avyayam
vivasvān manave prāha manur ikṣhvākave ’bravīt
source.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "I taught this imperishable Yoga to Vivasvan; he then told it to Manu; Manu proclaimed it to Ikshvaku.

simpleVersion: This, handed down in regular succession by the royal sages, was known, This Yoga, however, has been lost here over time, O Parantapa
explanation: In simple terms, This, handed down in regular succession by the royal sages, was known. This Yoga, however, has been lost here over time, O Parantapa (burner of the foes).

source.sanskrit:
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः।

स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप।।4.2।।
source.transliteration:
evaṁ paramparā-prāptam imaṁ rājarṣhayo viduḥ
sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣhṭaḥ parantapa
source.translation: This, handed down in regular succession by the royal sages, was known. This Yoga, however, has been lost here over time, O Parantapa (burner of the foes).

simpleVersion: That same ancient yoga has been today taught to you by me, for you are my devotee and my friend
explanation: In simple terms, That same ancient yoga has been today taught to you by me, for you are my devotee and my friend; it is the supreme secret.

source.sanskrit:
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः।

भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम्।।4.3।।
source.transliteration:
sa evāyaṁ mayā te ’dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ
bhakto ’si me sakhā cheti rahasyaṁ hyetad uttamam
source.translation: That same ancient yoga has been today taught to you by me, for you are my devotee and my friend; it is the supreme secret.

simpleVersion: Arjuna says later was your birth, and prior to it was the birth of Vivasvan
explanation: In simple terms, Arjuna said, "Later was your birth, and prior to it was the birth of Vivasvan (the Sun); how am I to understand that Thou hast taught this Yoga from the beginning?"

source.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः।

कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति।।4.4।।
source.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
aparaṁ bhavato janma paraṁ janma vivasvataḥ
katham etad vijānīyāṁ tvam ādau proktavān iti
source.translation: Arjuna said, "Later was Thy birth, and prior to it was the birth of Vivasvan (the Sun); how am I to understand that Thou hast taught this Yoga from the beginning?"

simpleVersion: Krishna says many births of Mine have passed, as well as of thine, O Arjuna, I know them all, but you knowest not, O Parantapa
explanation: In simple terms, The Blessed Lord said, "Many births of Mine have passed, as well as of thine, O Arjuna; I know them all, but you knowest not, O Parantapa (scorcher of foes)."

source.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन।

तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप।।4.5।।
source.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava chārjuna
tānyahaṁ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṁ vettha parantapa
source.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "Many births of Mine have passed, as well as of thine, O Arjuna; I know them all, but thou knowest not, O Parantapa (scorcher of foes)."

simpleVersion: Though I am unborn and of imperishable nature, and yough I am the Lord of all beings, yet, governing my own nature
explanation: In simple terms, Though I am unborn and of imperishable nature, and yough I am the Lord of all beings, yet, governing my own nature, I am born by my own Maya.

source.sanskrit:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन्।

प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया।।4.6।।
source.transliteration:
ajo ’pi sannavyayātmā bhūtānām īśhvaro ’pi san
prakṛitiṁ svām adhiṣhṭhāya sambhavāmyātma-māyayā
source.translation: Though I am unborn and of imperishable nature, and though I am the Lord of all beings, yet, governing my own nature, I am born by my own Maya.

simpleVersion: Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and an increase of unrighteousness, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself
explanation: In simple terms, Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and an increase of unrighteousness, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.

source.sanskrit:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।

अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम्।।4.7।।
source.transliteration:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata
abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛijāmyaham
source.translation: Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and an increase of unrighteousness, O Arjuna, then I manifest Myself.

simpleVersion: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the establishment of righteousness, I am born in every age
explanation: In simple terms, For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the establishment of righteousness, I am born in every age.

source.sanskrit:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।

धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे।।4.8।।
source.transliteration:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśhāya cha duṣhkṛitām
dharma-sansthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge
source.translation: For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the establishment of righteousness, I am born in every age.

simpleVersion: He who thus knows, in their true light, My divine birth and actions, having abandoned the body, is not born again
explanation: In simple terms, He who thus knows, in their true light, My divine birth and actions, having abandoned the body, is not born again; he comes to Me, O Arjuna.

source.sanskrit:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।

त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन।।4.9।।
source.transliteration:
janma karma cha me divyam evaṁ yo vetti tattvataḥ
tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti mām eti so ’rjuna
source.translation: He who thus knows, in their true light, My divine birth and actions, having abandoned the body, is not born again; he comes to Me, O Arjuna.

simpleVersion: Freed from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, purified by the fire of knowledge, many have attained My Being
explanation: In simple terms, Freed from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, purified by the fire of knowledge, many have attained My Being.

source.sanskrit:
वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः।

बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः।।4.10।।
source.transliteration:
vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhā man-mayā mām upāśhritāḥ
bahavo jñāna-tapasā pūtā mad-bhāvam āgatāḥ
source.translation: Freed from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, purified by the fire of knowledge, many have attained My Being.

simpleVersion: In whatever way men approach Me, even so do I reward them, My path do men tread in all ways, O Arjuna
explanation: In simple terms, In whatever way men approach Me, even so do I reward them; My path do men tread in all ways, O Arjuna.

source.sanskrit:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम्।

मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।4.11।।
source.transliteration:
ye yathā māṁ prapadyante tāns tathaiva bhajāmyaham
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣhyāḥ pārtha sarvaśhaḥ
source.translation: In whatever way men approach Me, even so do I reward them; My path do men tread in all ways, O Arjuna.

simpleVersion: Those who long for success in action in this world sacrifice to the gods, for success is quickly attained by men through action
explanation: In simple terms, Those who long for success in action in this world sacrifice to the gods; for success is quickly attained by men through action.

source.sanskrit:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः।

क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा।।4.12।।
source.transliteration:
kāṅkṣhantaḥ karmaṇāṁ siddhiṁ yajanta iha devatāḥ
kṣhipraṁ hi mānuṣhe loke siddhir bhavati karmajā
source.translation: Those who long for success in action in this world sacrifice to the gods; for success is quickly attained by men through action.

simpleVersion: The fourfold caste has been created by Me according to the differentiation of Guna and Karma, yough I am the author of it
explanation: In simple terms, The fourfold caste has been created by Me according to the differentiation of Guna and Karma; yough I am the author of it, know Me as non-doer and immutable.

source.sanskrit:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः।

तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम्।।4.13।।
source.transliteration:
chātur-varṇyaṁ mayā sṛiṣhṭaṁ guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśhaḥ
tasya kartāram api māṁ viddhyakartāram avyayam
source.translation: The fourfold caste has been created by Me according to the differentiation of Guna and Karma; though I am the author of it, know Me as non-doer and immutable.

simpleVersion: Actions do not taint Me, nor do I have a desire for the fruit of actions
explanation: In simple terms, Actions do not taint Me, nor do I have a desire for the fruit of actions. He who knows Me thus is not bound by actions.

source.sanskrit:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा।

इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते।।4.14।।
source.transliteration:
na māṁ karmāṇi limpanti na me karma-phale spṛihā
iti māṁ yo ’bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badhyate
source.translation: Actions do not taint Me, nor do I have a desire for the fruit of actions. He who knows Me thus is not bound by actions.

simpleVersion: Having known this, the ancient seekers of freedom also performed action, therefore, do you also perform action
explanation: In simple terms, Having known this, the ancient seekers of freedom also performed action; therefore, do you also perform action, as the ancients did in days of yore.

source.sanskrit:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः।

कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम्।।4.15।।
source.transliteration:
evaṁ jñātvā kṛitaṁ karma pūrvair api mumukṣhubhiḥ
kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṁ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṁ kṛitam
source.translation: Having known this, the ancient seekers of freedom also performed action; therefore, do thou also perform action, as the ancients did in days of yore.

simpleVersion: What is action?, What is inaction?, Even the wise are confused about this, Therefore, I shall teach you the nature of action and inaction
explanation: In simple terms, What is action? What is inaction? Even the wise are confused about this. Therefore, I shall teach you the nature of action and inaction, by knowing which you will be liberated from the evil of Samsara, the wheel of birth and death.

source.sanskrit:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः।

तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्।।4.16।।
source.transliteration:
kiṁ karma kim akarmeti kavayo ’pyatra mohitāḥ
tat te karma pravakṣhyāmi yaj jñātvā mokṣhyase ’śhubhāt
source.translation: What is action? What is inaction? Even the wise are confused about this. Therefore, I shall teach you the nature of action and inaction, by knowing which you will be liberated from the evil of Samsara, the wheel of birth and death.

simpleVersion: For verily, the true nature of action enjoined by the scriptures should be known, as well as that of forbidden or unlawful action
explanation: In simple terms, For verily, the true nature of action enjoined by the scriptures should be known, as well as that of forbidden or unlawful action, and of inaction; the nature of action is hard to understand.

source.sanskrit:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः।

अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः।।4.17।।
source.transliteration:
karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṁ boddhavyaṁ cha vikarmaṇaḥ
akarmaṇaśh cha boddhavyaṁ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ
source.translation: For verily, the true nature of action enjoined by the scriptures should be known, as well as that of forbidden or unlawful action, and of inaction; the nature of action is hard to understand.

simpleVersion: He who sees inaction in action and action in inaction, he is wise among men, he is a yogi and performer of all actions
explanation: In simple terms, He who sees inaction in action and action in inaction, he is wise among men; he is a yogi and performer of all actions.

source.sanskrit:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः।

स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत्।।4.18।।
source.transliteration:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśhyed akarmaṇi cha karma yaḥ
sa buddhimān manuṣhyeṣhu sa yuktaḥ kṛitsna-karma-kṛit
source.translation: He who sees inaction in action and action in inaction, he is wise among men; he is a yogi and performer of all actions.

simpleVersion: He whose undertakings are all devoid of desires and selfish purposes, and whose actions have been burned by the fire of knowledge
explanation: In simple terms, He whose undertakings are all devoid of desires and selfish purposes, and whose actions have been burned by the fire of knowledge, the wise call him a sage.

source.sanskrit:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः।

ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः।।4.19।।
source.transliteration:
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāma-saṅkalpa-varjitāḥ
jñānāgni-dagdha-karmāṇaṁ tam āhuḥ paṇḍitaṁ budhāḥ
source.translation: He whose undertakings are all devoid of desires and selfish purposes, and whose actions have been burned by the fire of knowledge, the wise call him a sage.

simpleVersion: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of the action, ever content, depending on nothing
explanation: In simple terms, Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of the action, ever content, depending on nothing, he does not do anything even while being engaged in activity.

source.sanskrit:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः।

कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः।।4.20।।
source.transliteration:
tyaktvā karma-phalāsaṅgaṁ nitya-tṛipto nirāśhrayaḥ
karmaṇyabhipravṛitto ’pi naiva kiñchit karoti saḥ
source.translation: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of the action, ever content, depending on nothing, he does not do anything even while being engaged in activity.

simpleVersion: Wiyout hope, controlling the mind and the self, having abandoned all covetousness, and performing only bodily actions, one incurs no sin
explanation: In simple terms, Wiyout hope, controlling the mind and the self, having abandoned all covetousness, and performing only bodily actions, one incurs no sin.

source.sanskrit:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः।

शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्।।4.21।।
source.transliteration:
nirāśhīr yata-chittātmā tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ
śhārīraṁ kevalaṁ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣham
source.translation: Without hope, controlling the mind and the self, having abandoned all covetousness, and performing only bodily actions, one incurs no sin.

simpleVersion: Content with what comes to him wiyout effort, free from the pairs of opposites and envy, even-minded in success and failure
explanation: In simple terms, Content with what comes to him wiyout effort, free from the pairs of opposites and envy, even-minded in success and failure, he acts yet is not bound.

source.sanskrit:
यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः।

समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते।।4.22।।
source.transliteration:
yadṛichchhā-lābha-santuṣhṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ
samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau cha kṛitvāpi na nibadhyate
source.translation: Content with what comes to him without effort, free from the pairs of opposites and envy, even-minded in success and failure, he acts yet is not bound.

simpleVersion: To one who is devoid of attachment, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, and who works for the sake of sacrifice
explanation: In simple terms, To one who is devoid of attachment, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, and who works for the sake of sacrifice (for the sake of God), the whole action is dissolved.

source.sanskrit:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः।

यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते।।4.23।।
source.transliteration:
gata-saṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthita-chetasaḥ
yajñāyācharataḥ karma samagraṁ pravilīyate
source.translation: To one who is devoid of attachment, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, and who works for the sake of sacrifice (for the sake of God), the whole action is dissolved.

simpleVersion: Brahman is the oblation, Brahman is the melted butter, by Brahman is the oblation poured into the fire of Brahman
explanation: In simple terms, Brahman is the oblation; Brahman is the melted butter (ghee); by Brahman is the oblation poured into the fire of Brahman; Brahman indeed shall be attained by one who always sees Brahman in action.

source.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्।

ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना।।4.24।।
source.transliteration:
brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṁ brahma-karma-samādhinā
source.translation: Brahman is the oblation; Brahman is the melted butter (ghee); by Brahman is the oblation poured into the fire of Brahman; Brahman indeed shall be attained by one who always sees Brahman in action.

simpleVersion: Some yogis perform sacrifice to the gods alone, while others, who have realized the Self
explanation: In simple terms, Some yogis perform sacrifice to the gods alone; while others, who have realized the Self, offer the Self as sacrifice in the fire of Brahman alone.

source.sanskrit:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते।

ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति।।4.25।।
source.transliteration:
daivam evāpare yajñaṁ yoginaḥ paryupāsate
brahmāgnāvapare yajñaṁ yajñenaivopajuhvati
source.translation: Some yogis perform sacrifice to the gods alone; while others, who have realized the Self, offer the Self as sacrifice in the fire of Brahman alone.

simpleVersion: Some again offer the organ of hearing and other senses as a sacrifice in the fire of restraint
explanation: In simple terms, Some again offer the organ of hearing and other senses as a sacrifice in the fire of restraint; others offer sound and other objects of the senses as a sacrifice in the fire of the senses.

source.sanskrit:
श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति।

शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति।।4.26।।
source.transliteration:
śhrotrādīnīndriyāṇyanye sanyamāgniṣhu juhvati
śhabdādīn viṣhayānanya indriyāgniṣhu juhvati
source.translation: Some again offer the organ of hearing and other senses as a sacrifice in the fire of restraint; others offer sound and other objects of the senses as a sacrifice in the fire of the senses.

simpleVersion: Others again sacrifice all the functions of the senses and those of the breath in the fire of the Yoga of self-restraint
explanation: In simple terms, Others again sacrifice all the functions of the senses and those of the breath (vital energy, or Prana) in the fire of the Yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.

source.sanskrit:
सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे।

आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते।।4.27।।
source.transliteration:
sarvāṇīndriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi chāpare
ātma-sanyama-yogāgnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite
source.translation: Others again sacrifice all the functions of the senses and those of the breath (vital energy, or Prana) in the fire of the Yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.

simpleVersion: Others again offer wealth, austerity, and Yoga as sacrifice
explanation: In simple terms, Others again offer wealth, austerity, and Yoga as sacrifice, while ascetics of self-restraint and rigid vows offer the study of scriptures and knowledge as sacrifice.

source.sanskrit:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे।

स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः।।4.28।।
source.transliteration:
dravya-yajñās tapo-yajñā yoga-yajñās tathāpare
swādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāśh cha yatayaḥ sanśhita-vratāḥ
source.translation: Others again offer wealth, austerity, and Yoga as sacrifice, while ascetics of self-restraint and rigid vows offer the study of scriptures and knowledge as sacrifice.

simpleVersion: Others offer as sacrifice the outgoing breath into the incoming, and the incoming into the outgoing
explanation: In simple terms, Others offer as sacrifice the outgoing breath into the incoming, and the incoming into the outgoing, restraining the flow of the outgoing and the incoming breaths, solely absorbed in the restraint of the breath.

source.sanskrit:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राण प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे।

प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः।।4.29।।
source.transliteration:
apāne juhvati prāṇaṁ prāṇe ’pānaṁ tathāpare
prāṇāpāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ
 apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣhu juhvati
sarve ’pyete yajña-vido yajña-kṣhapita-kalmaṣhāḥ
source.translation: Others offer as sacrifice the outgoing breath into the incoming, and the incoming into the outgoing, restraining the flow of the outgoing and the incoming breaths, solely absorbed in the restraint of the breath.

simpleVersion: Others who regulate their diet offer life-breaths in each life-breath, All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose sins are destroyed through sacrifice
explanation: In simple terms, Others who regulate their diet offer life-breaths in each life-breath. All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose sins are destroyed through sacrifice.

source.sanskrit:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति।

सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः।।4.30।।
source.transliteration:
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān  prāṇeṣu juhvati

sarve py 'ete yajña-vido yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ
source.translation: Others who regulate their diet offer life-breaths in each life-breath. All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose sins are destroyed through sacrifice.

simpleVersion: Those who eat the remnants of the sacrifice, which are like nectar, go to the eternal Brahman
explanation: In simple terms, Those who eat the remnants of the sacrifice, which are like nectar, go to the eternal Brahman. This world is not for the one who does not perform sacrifice; how then can they have the other, O Arjuna?

source.sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम्।

नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतो़ऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम।।4.31।।
source.transliteration:
yajña-śhiṣhṭāmṛita-bhujo yānti brahma sanātanam
nāyaṁ loko ’styayajñasya kuto ’nyaḥ kuru-sattama
source.translation: Those who eat the remnants of the sacrifice, which are like nectar, go to the eternal Brahman. This world is not for the one who does not perform sacrifice; how then can they have the other, O Arjuna?

simpleVersion: Thus, manifold sacrifices are spread out before Brahman at the face of Brahman, Know them all to be born of action, and thus knowing
explanation: In simple terms, Thus, manifold sacrifices are spread out before Brahman at the face of Brahman. Know them all to be born of action, and thus knowing, you shall be liberated.

source.sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे।

कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे।।4.32।।
source.transliteration:
evaṁ bahu-vidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe
karma-jān viddhi tān sarvān evaṁ jñātvā vimokṣhyase
source.translation: Thus, manifold sacrifices are spread out before Brahman at the face of Brahman. Know them all to be born of action, and thus knowing, you shall be liberated.

simpleVersion: Superior is wisdom-sacrifice to the sacrifice with objects, O Parantapa, All actions in their entirety, O Arjuna, culminate in knowledge
explanation: In simple terms, Superior is wisdom-sacrifice to the sacrifice with objects, O Parantapa (scorcher of the foes). All actions in their entirety, O Arjuna, culminate in knowledge.

source.sanskrit:
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप।

सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते।।4.33।।
source.transliteration:
śhreyān dravya-mayād yajñāj jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa
sarvaṁ karmākhilaṁ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate
source.translation: Superior is wisdom-sacrifice to the sacrifice with objects, O Parantapa (scorcher of the foes). All actions in their entirety, O Arjuna, culminate in knowledge.

simpleVersion: Know that the wise who have realized the truth will instruct you in that knowledge through long prostration, supplication, and service
explanation: In simple terms, Know that the wise who have realized the truth will instruct you in that knowledge through long prostration, supplication, and service.

source.sanskrit:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया।

उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः।।4.34।।
source.transliteration:
tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśhnena sevayā
upadekṣhyanti te jñānaṁ jñāninas tattva-darśhinaḥ
source.translation: Know that the wise who have realized the truth will instruct thee in that knowledge through long prostration, supplication, and service.

simpleVersion: Knowing that you shalt not, O Arjuna, again be deluded like this
explanation: In simple terms, Knowing that you shalt not, O Arjuna, again be deluded like this; and by that you shalt see all beings in yourself and also in me.

source.sanskrit:
यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव।

येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि।।4.35।।
source.transliteration:
yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṁ yāsyasi pāṇḍava
yena bhūtānyaśheṣheṇa drakṣhyasyātmanyatho mayi
source.translation: Knowing that thou shalt not, O Arjuna, again be deluded like this; and by that thou shalt see all beings in thyself and also in me.

simpleVersion: Even if you art the most sinful of all sinners, yet you shalt surely cross over all sins by the raft of knowledge
explanation: In simple terms, Even if you art the most sinful of all sinners, yet you shalt surely cross over all sins by the raft of knowledge.

source.sanskrit:
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः।

सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि।।4.36।।
source.transliteration:
api ched asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛit-tamaḥ
sarvaṁ jñāna-plavenaiva vṛijinaṁ santariṣhyasi
source.translation: Even if thou art the most sinful of all sinners, yet thou shalt surely cross over all sins by the raft of knowledge.

simpleVersion: As the blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ash
explanation: In simple terms, As the blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ash.

source.sanskrit:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन।

ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा।।4.37।।
source.transliteration:
yathaidhānsi samiddho ’gnir bhasma-sāt kurute ’rjuna
jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasma-sāt kurute tathā
source.translation: As the blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ash.

simpleVersion: Verily, there is no purifier in this world like knowledge, He who is perfected in Yoga finds it within the Self in due time
explanation: In simple terms, Verily, there is no purifier in this world like knowledge. He who is perfected in Yoga finds it within the Self in due time.

source.sanskrit:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते।

तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति।।4.38।।
source.transliteration:
na hi jñānena sadṛiśhaṁ pavitramiha vidyate
tatsvayaṁ yogasansiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati
source.translation: Verily, there is no purifier in this world like knowledge. He who is perfected in Yoga finds it within the Self in due time.

simpleVersion: The one who is full of faith, devoted to it, and has subdued their senses obtains this knowledge, and upon obtaining the knowledge
explanation: In simple terms, The one who is full of faith, devoted to it, and has subdued their senses obtains this knowledge; and upon obtaining the knowledge, they attain the supreme peace immediately.

source.sanskrit:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः।

ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति।।4.39।।
source.transliteration:
śhraddhāvān labhate jñānaṁ tat-paraḥ sanyatendriyaḥ
jñānaṁ labdhvā parāṁ śhāntim achireṇādhigachchhati
source.translation: The one who is full of faith, devoted to it, and has subdued their senses obtains this knowledge; and upon obtaining the knowledge, they attain the supreme peace immediately.

simpleVersion: The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting self go to destruction, there is neither this world nor the other
explanation: In simple terms, The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting self go to destruction; there is neither this world nor the other, nor happiness for the doubting one.

source.sanskrit:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति।

नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः।।4.40।।
source.transliteration:
ajñaśh chāśhraddadhānaśh cha sanśhayātmā vinaśhyati
nāyaṁ loko ’sti na paro na sukhaṁ sanśhayātmanaḥ
source.translation: The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting self go to destruction; there is neither this world nor the other, nor happiness for the doubting one.

simpleVersion: He who has renounced actions through Yoga, whose doubts have been dispelled by knowledge
explanation: In simple terms, He who has renounced actions through Yoga, whose doubts have been dispelled by knowledge, and who is self-possessed—such a one is not bound by actions, O Arjuna.

source.sanskrit:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम्।

आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय।।4.41।।
source.transliteration:
yoga-sannyasta-karmāṇaṁ jñāna-sañchhinna-sanśhayam
ātmavantaṁ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya
source.translation: He who has renounced actions through Yoga, whose doubts have been dispelled by knowledge, and who is self-possessed—such a one is not bound by actions, O Arjuna.

simpleVersion: Therefore, with the sword of knowledge, cut asunder the doubt of the self, born of ignorance, residing in your heart
explanation: In simple terms, Therefore, with the sword of knowledge (of the Self), cut asunder the doubt of the self, born of ignorance, residing in your heart, and take refuge in Yoga. Arise, O Arjuna!

source.sanskrit:
तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः।

छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत।।4.42।।
source.transliteration:
tasmād ajñāna-sambhūtaṁ hṛit-sthaṁ jñānāsinātmanaḥ
chhittvainaṁ sanśhayaṁ yogam ātiṣhṭhottiṣhṭha bhārata
source.translation: Therefore, with the sword of knowledge (of the Self), cut asunder the doubt of the self, born of ignorance, residing in your heart, and take refuge in Yoga. Arise, O Arjuna!

simpleVersion: Arjuna says o Krishna, you praise renunciation of actions and also yoga, Please tell me conclusively which is better of the two
explanation: In simple terms, Arjuna said, "O Krishna, you praise renunciation of actions and also yoga. Please tell me conclusively which is better of the two."

source.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच

संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि।

यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्िचतम्।।5.1।।
source.transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
sannyāsaṁ karmaṇāṁ kṛiṣhṇa punar yogaṁ cha śhansasi
yach chhreya etayor ekaṁ tan me brūhi su-niśhchitam
source.translation: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, you praise renunciation of actions and also yoga. Please tell me conclusively which is better of the two."

simpleVersion: Krishna says renunciation and the Yoga of action both lead to the highest bliss, but of the two
explanation: In simple terms, The Blessed Lord said, "Renunciation and the Yoga of action both lead to the highest bliss; but of the two, the Yoga of action is superior to the renunciation of action."

source.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच

संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ।

तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते।।5.2।।
source.transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
sannyāsaḥ karma-yogaśh cha niḥśhreyasa-karāvubhau
tayos tu karma-sannyāsāt karma-yogo viśhiṣhyate
source.translation: The Blessed Lord said, "Renunciation and the Yoga of action both lead to the highest bliss; but of the two, the Yoga of action is superior to the renunciation of action."

simpleVersion: He should be known as a perpetual Sannyasi who neither hates nor desires, for, free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed Arjuna
explanation: In simple terms, He should be known as a perpetual Sannyasi who neither hates nor desires; for, free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed Arjuna, he is easily freed from bondage.

source.sanskrit:
ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति।

निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते।।5.3।।
source.transliteration:
jñeyaḥ sa nitya-sannyāsī yo na dveṣhṭi na kāṅkṣhati
nirdvandvo hi mahā-bāho sukhaṁ bandhāt pramuchyate
source.translation: He should be known as a perpetual Sannyasi who neither hates nor desires; for, free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed Arjuna, he is easily freed from bondage.

simpleVersion: Children, not the wise, speak of knowledge and the Yoga of action, or the performance of action, as yough they are distinct and different
explanation: In simple terms, Children, not the wise, speak of knowledge and the Yoga of action, or the performance of action, as yough they are distinct and different; he who is truly established in one, obtains the fruits of both.

source.sanskrit:
सांख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः।

एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम्।।5.4।।
source.transliteration:
sānkhya-yogau pṛithag bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ
ekamapyāsthitaḥ samyag ubhayor vindate phalam
source.translation: Children, not the wise, speak of knowledge and the Yoga of action, or the performance of action, as though they are distinct and different; he who is truly established in one, obtains the fruits of both.

simpleVersion: That place which is reached by the Sankhyas or the Jnanis is also reached by the Yogis
explanation: In simple terms, That place which is reached by the Sankhyas or the Jnanis is also reached by the Yogis (Karma Yogis). He who sees knowledge and the performance of action (Karma Yoga) as one, sees truly.

source.sanskrit:
यत्सांख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते।

एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति।।5.5।।
source.transliteration:
yat sānkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṁ tad yogair api gamyate
ekaṁ sānkhyaṁ cha yogaṁ cha yaḥ paśhyati sa paśhyati
source.translation: That place which is reached by the Sankhyas or the Jnanis is also reached by the Yogis (Karma Yogis). He who sees knowledge and the performance of action (Karma Yoga) as one, sees truly.

simpleVersion: But, O mighty-armed Arjuna, renunciation is hard to attain wiyout Yoga, the sage who is in harmony with Yoga quickly goes to Brahman
explanation: In simple terms, But, O mighty-armed Arjuna, renunciation is hard to attain wiyout Yoga; the sage who is in harmony with Yoga quickly goes to Brahman.

source.sanskrit:
संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः।

योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति।।5.6।।
source.transliteration:
sannyāsas tu mahā-bāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ
yoga-yukto munir brahma na chireṇādhigachchhati
source.translation: But, O mighty-armed Arjuna, renunciation is hard to attain without Yoga; the sage who is in harmony with Yoga quickly goes to Brahman.

simpleVersion: He who is devoted to the path of action, whose mind is pure, who has conquered the self, who has subdued his senses
explanation: In simple terms, He who is devoted to the path of action, whose mind is pure, who has conquered the self, who has subdued his senses, and who realizes his Self as the Self in all beings, yough acting, is not tainted.

source.sanskrit:
योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः।

सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते।।5.7।।
source.transliteration:
yoga-yukto viśhuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ
sarva-bhūtātma-bhūtātmā kurvann api na lipyate
source.translation: He who is devoted to the path of action, whose mind is pure, who has conquered the self, who has subdued his senses, and who realizes his Self as the Self in all beings, though acting, is not tainted.

simpleVersion: I do nothing at all," thus would the harmonized knower of Truth think, seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping, and breathing
explanation: In simple terms, I do nothing at all," thus would the harmonized knower of Truth think, seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping, and breathing.

source.sanskrit:
नैव किंचित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित्।

पश्यन् श्रृणवन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन् श्वसन्।।5.8।।
source.transliteration:
naiva kiñchit karomīti yukto manyeta tattva-vit
paśhyañ śhṛiṇvan spṛiśhañjighrann aśhnangachchhan svapañśhvasan
 pralapan visṛijan gṛihṇann unmiṣhan nimiṣhann api
indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣhu vartanta iti dhārayan
source.translation: I do nothing at all," thus would the harmonized knower of Truth think, seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping, and breathing.

simpleVersion: Speaking, letting go, seizing, opening, and closing the eyes, one should be convinced that the senses move among the sense-objects
explanation: In simple terms, Speaking, letting go, seizing, opening, and closing the eyes, one should be convinced that the senses move among the sense-objects.

source.sanskrit:
प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन्।।5.9।।
source.transliteration: pralapan visṛjan gṛhṇann unmiṣan nimiṣann api indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan
source.translation: Speaking, letting go, seizing, opening, and closing the eyes, one should be convinced that the senses move among the sense-objects.

simpleVersion: He who does actions, offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin
explanation: In simple terms, He who does actions, offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not tainted by water.

source.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः।

लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा।।5.10।।
source.transliteration:
brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ
lipyate na sa pāpena padma-patram ivāmbhasā
source.translation: He who does actions, offering them to Brahman and abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not tainted by water.

simpleVersion: Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform actions only through the body, mind, intellect, and even the senses, for the purification of the self
explanation: In simple terms, Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform actions only through the body, mind, intellect, and even the senses, for the purification of the self.

source.sanskrit:
कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि।

योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये।।5.11।।
source.transliteration:
kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalair indriyair api
yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṁ tyaktvātma-śhuddhaye
source.translation: Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform actions only through the body, mind, intellect, and even the senses, for the purification of the self.

simpleVersion: The one who is united having abandoned the fruit of action attains eternal peace, whereas the one who is not united
explanation: In simple terms, The one who is united (the well-poised or harmonized) having abandoned the fruit of action attains eternal peace; whereas the one who is not united (the unsteady or unbalanced), impelled by desire and attached to the fruit, is bound.

source.sanskrit:
युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम्।

अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते।।5.12।।
